Watzat?

A Québecois (or Cape Breton?) 3 parts reel named after a fiddler. Goes well after Andy Renwick’s Ferret, and before Big Mon. I think it’s on a Bottine Souriante CD.

Macdonald’s march

Sometimes has a fourth part to it. Pipe tune from Cape Breton usually played by fiddlers in the key of A . Quite popular in Quebec. Maybe La Bottine got it from the playing of Joe Cormier, thus your name for it.

MacDonald’s

The second of two tunes collected from Gina Le Faux way back when. Gina learned it from the playing of Cape Breton Fiddler, Joe Cormier. We also think that it is somewhere in Kerrs, when I find my copies (5 volumes) I will have a gander (hmm). (Great collection, many hidden gems lie within)

I play this with slight swing, but have left the dots unswung this time. It follows on from the Birthday reel, and the key change into A really lifts an already upbeat set.

Occasionally we put the two together and play them as a 4 parter when needing a 64 bar reel.

MacDonald’s

I transcribed this 4 part version (yes, it has the much sought-after 4th part!)
from the great fiddling of Becky Tracy on Nightingale’s
“Sometimes When The Moon Is High” CD. It’s the first track, played
at the end of a medley with Ballygow and The Bus Stop Reel.

The liner notes have only this to say:
“…MacDonald’s is a Scottish tune that comes to us via Cape Breton.”

This tune is related to a 3 part version of Joe Cormier’s;
https://thesession.org/tunes/5661
however this setting has a 4th part and the first 3 parts are different enough from
Joe Cormier’s that I believe it warrants its own entry.
I’ll let Jeremy have the final say; if he disagrees, I’ll post this version
at the end of the Joe Cormier’s page.
It’s a crackin‘ good tune; hope all y’all like it.

Re: Joe Cormier’s

MacDonald’s March was played by Joe Cormier (originally from Chéticamp, Cape Breton) on his 1977 album The Dances Down Home (Rounder 7004). A transcription in available on Paul Cranford’s site: https://www.cranfordpub.com/recordings/CormierDownHome.htm#Anchor
The tune was published in Kerr’s Merry Melodies, Bk.3 in the late 1800s.
The tune was picked, altered and called Reel de Jos Cormier by Quebec band Bottine Souriante on their 1987 Tout Comme Au Jour De L’An (Mille-Pattes ‎– MMPCD-2035) album. Their version can be heard at
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjnNfA9htq0

↳ Posted by Paul Fackler on November 3rd, 2020.

MacDonald’s, X:7

I heard this played at a session in early January and really liked it.
Two nineteenth century appearances in print are Ross’s Collection of Pipe Music (two parts) and Kerr’s Third Collection of Merry Melodies (three parts). Later printings, both three-parters, are in The Cape Breton Collection of Pipe Music by Barry Shears (1995) and The Cape Breton Fiddlers Collection (2007, as a reel).

I have based my setting very much on that of Barry Shears since he has an audio recording of the tune at: https://www.capebretonpiper.com/music-and-videos
He goes back to the first part on the repeat of the second part (although not shown in his score) and I feel inclined to do the same, but that’s not what was played in the early January session so I’m resisting so as to fit in with the other players.

↳ Posted by DonaldK on February 19th, 2023.

Macdonald’s, X:8

This is how I’ve been playing this march/reel recently.

It appeared in Ross‘ Collection of Pipe Music (1885?) as a two-part tune titled “The MacDonalds’ March”.
Around the same time (1879?) it turned up in Kerr’s Third Collection of Merry Melodies as a three-part tune with the same title but apostrophe moved - “The MacDonald’s March”.

Over a century later in 1995, it appeared in Barry Shears’ Cape Breton Collection of Pipe Music - three parts but losing the definite article in the title (MacDonald’s March) and Paul Cranford’s The Cape Breton Fiddlers Collection (page 7) in 2007.

The tune was used in the 1970’s and 80’s as the theme tune for CBC Sydney’s “Island Echoes” radio show.
It’s certainly associated with Joe Cormier as he recorded it three times on The Dances Down Home (1975), Chéticamp and Velvet Arm, Golden Hand.

You can hear a slightly different setting, as played by Maggie Sansone here:
https://youtu.be/ejZ12jL2Rmo?list=OLAK5uy_l3fvOqDIjRt7ns9MKD-mw4K2jXdz0-Syc&t=139

At some point a fourth part has been added as here (though it’s essentially the same tune):
https://thesession.org/tunes/10283

Haha! I should have read the post above by Paul Fackler.

I also find I have already posted this setting under MacDonald’s March:
https://thesession.org/tunes/8802

Crazy!
